title: High-altitude pulmonary edema is aggravated by risk loci and associated transcription factors in HIF-prolyl hydroxylases.
authors: Sharma, Kavita; Mishra, Aastha; Singh, Himanshu N; Parashar, Deepak; Alam, Perwez; Thinlas, Tashi; Mohammad, Ghulam; Kukreti, Ritushree; Syed, Mansoor Ali; Pasha, M A Qadar
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过遗传关联与实验验证发现HAPE风险位点影响EGLN1/HIF1AN表达，并鉴定等位基因特异性TF-DNA结合，辅以分子对接模拟，属于广义蛋白-DNA互作但以湿实验为主、AI/物理模拟深度有限。
abstract: High-altitude (HA, >2500 m) hypoxic exposure evokes several physiological processes that may be abetted by differential genetic distribution in sojourners, who are susceptible to various HA disorders, such as high-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE). The genetic variants in hypoxia-sensing genes influence the transcriptional output; however the functional role has not been investigated in HAPE. This study explored the two hypoxia-sensing genes, prolyl hydroxylase domain protein 2 (EGLN1) and factor inhibiting HIF-1alpha (HIF1AN) in HA adaptation and maladaptation in three well-characterized groups: highland natives, HAPE-free controls and HAPE-patients. The two genes were sequenced and subsequently validated through genotyping of significant single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), haplotyping and multifactor dimensionality reduction. Three EGLN1 SNPs rs1538664, rs479200 and rs480902 and their haplotypes emerged significant in HAPE. Blood gene expression and protein levels also differed significantly (P < 0.05) and correlated with clinical parameters and respective alleles. The RegulomeDB annotation exercises of the loci corroborated regulatory role. Allele-specific differential expression was evidenced by luciferase assay followed by electrophoretic mobility shift assay, liquid chromatography with tandem mass spectrometry and supershift assays, which confirmed allele-specific transcription factor (TF) binding of FUS RNA-binding protein (FUS) with rs1538664A, Rho GDP dissociation inhibitor 1 (ARHDGIA) with rs479200T and hypoxia upregulated protein 1 (HYOU1) with rs480902C. Docking simulation studies were in sync for the DNA-TF structural variations. There was strong networking among the TFs that revealed physiological consequences through relevant pathways. The two hydroxylases appear crucial in the regulation of hypoxia-inducible responses.
abstract_zh: 高海拔（HA，>2500 m）低氧暴露会引发多种生理过程，这些过程可能因旅居者的遗传分布差异而得到促进，而旅居者易患多种高海拔疾病，如高海拔肺水肿（HAPE）。缺氧感应基因中的遗传变异影响转录输出；然而，其功能作用在HAPE中尚未被研究。本研究探讨了两个缺氧感应基因——脯氨酰羟化酶结构域蛋白2（EGLN1）和缺氧诱导因子-1α抑制因子（HIF1AN）在三个特征明确的群体中的高海拔适应与不适应中的作用：高原土著居民、无HAPE对照组和HAPE患者。对这两个基因进行了测序，并通过显著单核苷酸多态性（SNPs）的基因分型、单倍型分析和多因子降维法进行了后续验证。三个EGLN1 SNP rs1538664、rs479200和rs480902及其单倍型在HAPE中表现出显著性。血液基因表达和蛋白质水平也显著不同（P < 0.05），并与临床参数及相应等位基因相关。RegulomeDB注释分析证实了这些位点的调控作用。等位基因特异性差异表达通过荧光素酶实验、电泳迁移率变动实验、液相色谱-串联质谱法和超迁移实验得到证实，这些实验确认了FUS RNA结合蛋白（FUS）与rs1538664A、Rho GDP解离抑制剂1（ARHDGIA）与rs479200T以及缺氧上调蛋白1（HYOU1）与rs480902C的等位基因特异性转录因子（TF）结合。对接模拟研究与DNA-TF结构变异相一致。这些转录因子之间存在强相互作用网络，通过相关途径揭示了生理后果。这两种羟化酶在缺氧诱导反应的调控中似乎至关重要。
